correctness.rationale: In RESULT.md 18–31, an all-positive realization preserves every source circuit; keeping all but one assignment in that circuit positive forces the remaining one, precluding shattering. Invertibility then gives target independence. Conversely, given p prescribed positives, invertible extensions act transitively on vectors outside the target span, so each forbidden equality has probability 1/(q^d-q^p). For p<k≤d and d≥2 the union bound is strictly less than one; p=k only requires extension of an isomorphism of subspaces. Ordering both independent tuples and dividing by k! counts supports; simultaneous basis extension proves purity, and the displayed nontransitive parallel pairs rule out a matroid. A fresh bounded Python calculation obtained (9,18) and connectivity in binary rank two, and (49,882,4704), connectivity, and GF(2) boundary ranks 48 and 834 in binary rank three. The resulting Betti numbers agree exactly.
residual_risks: The bounded check establishes only the stated small binary homology. The universal classification rests on the proof, and no claim is made about integral torsion or general homotopy type.
